tasks.title: Sum of two
tasks.statement: Write a function add that takes two i32 numbers and returns their sum.
tasks.hint: The last expression without a semicolon becomes the result: a + b

tasks.title: Square of a number
tasks.statement: Write a function square(x: i32) -> i32 that returns the square of the number.
tasks.hint: x * x — without return and without a semicolon.

tasks.title: Even number
tasks.statement: Write a function is_even(n: i32) -> bool: true for even numbers, including negative ones and zero.
tasks.hint: The remainder of division by 2 is zero. For negative n, n % 2 is also -1 or 0, so comparing with 0 works.

tasks.title: The larger of two
tasks.statement: Write a function max_of_two(a, b) that returns the larger of two i32 values. Use if–else as an expression.
tasks.hint: if a > b { a } else { b } — a block of expressions without semicolons.

tasks.title: Absolute difference
tasks.statement: Write a function abs_diff(a, b): the distance |a − b| between two i32 numbers. Do not use the built-in method — only if–else and subtraction.
tasks.hint: Subtract the smaller from the larger.

tasks.title: Area and perimeter
tasks.statement: Write two functions for a rectangle with integer sides: area(w, h) for the area and perimeter(w, h) for the perimeter.
tasks.hint: area: w * h; perimeter: 2 * (w + h).

tasks.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
tasks.statement: Write a function c_to_f(c: f64) -> f64: degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit using the formula c · 9 / 5 + 32.
tasks.hint: The numbers in the formula are float literals: 9.0, 5.0, 32.0.

tasks.title: Greeting
tasks.statement: Write a function greet(name: &str) -> String that returns the string «Привет, <name>!» (the word «Привет» exactly as written, then the name). Use the format! macro.
tasks.hint: format!("Привет, {}!", name) returns a String instead of printing.

tasks.title: Quotient and remainder
tasks.statement: Write a function divmod(a, b) -> (i32, i32): the quotient and the remainder of dividing a by b (b > 0, a ≥ 0).
tasks.hint: Return the tuple (a / b, a % b).

tasks.title: Smallest and largest
tasks.statement: Write a function min_max(a, b, c) -> (i32, i32): the smallest and the largest of three numbers. You may use the methods a.min(b) and a.max(b).
tasks.hint: a.min(b).min(c) and a.max(b).max(c)

tasks.title: Sign of a number
tasks.statement: Write a function sign(n: i32) -> i32: 1 for positive numbers, -1 for negative ones, 0 for zero. Use a single if – else if – else expression.
tasks.hint: A chain if … else if … else is one expression; all branches are i32.

tasks.title: Clamp to a range
tasks.statement: Write a function clamp(x, lo, hi): if x is less than lo, return lo; if greater than hi, return hi; otherwise x. Use early return.
tasks.hint: Two early returns, then x as the final expression.

tasks.title: Factorial
tasks.statement: Write a function fact(n: u64) -> u64: the factorial n! (0! = 1). Solve it with recursion.
tasks.hint: Base case: n ≤ 1 → 1. Step: n * fact(n - 1).

tasks.title: Fibonacci numbers
tasks.statement: Write a function fib(n: u32) -> u64 using recursion: fib(0) = 0, fib(1) = 1, fib(n) = fib(n−1) + fib(n−2).
tasks.hint: For n < 2 the result equals n itself; convert it to u64 with as.

tasks.title: GCD by recursion
tasks.statement: Write a function gcd(a: u32, b: u32) -> u32 — the greatest common divisor by Euclid's algorithm: gcd(a, 0) = a, otherwise gcd(b, a % b).
tasks.hint: Recursion reduces the pair (a, b) to (b, a % b) until b becomes zero.

tasks.title: Raising to a power
tasks.statement: Write a function power(base: i64, exp: u32) -> i64 using recursion, without pow: power(x, 0) = 1, power(x, n) = x · power(x, n−1).
tasks.hint: Base case: exp == 0 → 1.

tasks.title: Sum up to n
tasks.statement: Write a function sum_to(n: u32) -> u32 using recursion: 1 + 2 + … + n (sum_to(0) = 0).
tasks.hint: n + sum_to(n - 1)

tasks.title: Leap year
tasks.statement: Write a function is_leap(year: u32) -> bool: a year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100 but not by 400.
tasks.hint: The whole condition is a single boolean expression with &&, ||.

tasks.title: Within a range
tasks.statement: Write a function in_range(x, lo, hi) -> bool: true if lo ≤ x ≤ hi (the bounds are included).
tasks.hint: x >= lo && x <= hi

tasks.title: Swap
tasks.statement: Write a function swap(p: (i32, i32)) -> (i32, i32) that returns the pair with its elements swapped.
tasks.hint: Access by index: p.0 and p.1; return a new tuple.

tasks.title: Sum and average
tasks.statement: Write a function stats(a, b, c) -> (i32, f64): the sum of three numbers and their arithmetic mean (as f64).
tasks.hint: First sum, then the tuple (sum, sum as f64 / 3.0).

tasks.title: Sum of digits
tasks.statement: Write a function digit_sum(n: u32) -> u32 using recursion: the sum of the decimal digits of a number. digit_sum(0) = 0, otherwise n % 10 + digit_sum(n / 10).
tasks.hint: The last digit is n % 10, the rest is n / 10.

tasks.title: Number of digits
tasks.statement: Write a function count_digits(n: u64) -> u32: how many digits are in the decimal representation of n (for 0 — one digit).
tasks.hint: If the number is less than 10, it is one digit; otherwise 1 plus the number of digits in n / 10.

tasks.title: Hypotenuse
tasks.statement: Write a function hypot(a: f64, b: f64) -> f64: the length of the hypotenuse √(a² + b²).
tasks.hint: (a * a + b * b).sqrt()

tasks.title: Fix it: no result type
tasks.statement: The function double must return the doubled number, but the signature has no result type. Fix the signature — you don't need to change the body.
tasks.hint: Add -> i32 after the parameter parentheses.

tasks.title: Fix it: extra semicolon
tasks.statement: The function cube returns () instead of i32 because of the semicolon at the end. Fix it.
tasks.hint: Remove the ; on the last line.

tasks.title: Fix it: integer and float
tasks.statement: The function average must return the mean of two integers as f64, but (a + b) is an integer, and it has to be divided by the float 2.0. Fix the function body: average(3, 4) = 3.5.
tasks.hint: The sum must be converted to f64: (a + b) as f64 / 2.0

tasks.title: Functions together
tasks.statement: The code already has a function add. Write triple(x) that returns 3·x using only add (no * operation).
tasks.hint: add(add(x, x), x) — a call inside a call.

tasks.title: FizzBuzz for one number
tasks.statement: Write a function fizz(n: u32) -> String: «FizzBuzz» if n is divisible by 15, «Fizz» if by 3, «Buzz» if by 5, otherwise the number itself as a string. Use a single if – else if expression.
tasks.hint: Check divisibility by 15 first. n.to_string() turns a number into a string.

tasks.title: BMI category
tasks.statement: Write a function category(bmi: f64) -> &'static str: «недостаток» if bmi < 18.5, «норма» if bmi < 25.0, «избыток» if bmi < 30.0, otherwise «ожирение».
tasks.hint: String literals are &'static str: you can return them straight from the branches.
